Governance review

Treasury and counterparties

A classification-first review of grants, compensation, OTC, validator transfers and deliverables.

Start with classification

Gross flow is not personal income.

The reviewed records mix grants, scheduled compensation, reimbursements, protocol operations, locked allocations and asset exchanges. Each needs different evidence. A large LUNA receipt may be an OTC trade; a contract receipt may be liquidity deployment; a scheduled claim may relate to an earlier entitlement period.

Do not add upstream grants and downstream distributions twice. Do not describe recurring transfers as vote buying without an agreement, communications or other direct evidence.

Director compensation and selective October schedules

The 2026 coverage window records 57,096 USDC to MB, 66,480 USDC to Vini and 46,745.70 USDC to Rose under the report’s classifications. Vini’s total includes a 16,900-USDC audit payment and recurring infra payments. Rose separately received 237,323.047934 LUNA in an OTC trade supplying approximately 0.19657723 WBTC; that is not compensation.

October actions 118–120 created new Stewardship payments for 0xphilipp, Rose and MB, but not Vini. Separate infra actions continued. The chain record does not explain the omission.

OTC and related-party execution

The 50-weight ERIS signer received 795,991.566014 LUNA through Treasury offers 91, 106 and 111. The checked messages are execute_otc, so these are asset exchanges, not salary. The governance questions are price fairness, approval, disclosure and execution quality.

Other large OTC recipients must likewise be valued using the asset they supplied and execution-time prices. LUNA totals alone do not establish expense, gain or loss.

A forensic accountant’s next requests

  1. Complete action exports: recipient, entitlement period, approval, claim, cancellation and transaction.
  2. Contracts, invoices and pricing for monthly validator transfers and the ERIS invoice to Rebel.
  3. Statements of work, competing quotes where relevant, measurable deliverables and independent acceptance.
  4. Related-party OTC terms, supplied assets, market-rate checks and execution timestamps.
  5. Beneficiary/decider overlap and recusal records for A159, A249, A266 and A271.
  6. Admin and owner powers over recipients, schedules, fees, code and future voting.
  7. Account continuity without assuming exclusive key custody; reconcile current and predecessor role wallets.
  8. Direct wallet-flow graphs that distinguish native transfers, CW20 transfers, contract operations and module accounts.
